comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C40-C41 regarding B. hermsii infection validation. Both evaluations find these claims supported, with peer reviewers specifically praising the use of multiple pathogens (LPS and B. hermsii) as a study strength.

Perfect agreement on claims C19-C21 regarding PCA analysis and transcriptomic variability in deermice. Both evaluations find these claims supported without concerns, though OpenEval notes the biological significance requires further investigation.

Perfect agreement on methodological claims C73-C81. Both evaluations affirm the methods as appropriate and well-documented, with peer reviewers specifically commending the use of outbred mice and noting that concerns about sample sizes and sex differences were addressed.

Strong agreement on contextual/discussion claims C52-C66 (and C71-C72 in OpenEval). Both evaluations accept these literature-based claims as appropriate context, with peer reviewers describing the work as 'well researched' and conclusions as 'thoughtful.'

Strong agreement on background claims C1-C2 and C8-C10 (C9-C10 overlap). Both evaluations accept these as established literature context, with peer reviewers affirming the relevance of P. leucopus as a reservoir species.
Strong agreement on hematology claims C14-C18. Both evaluations find these claims supported, with peer reviewers noting that initial concerns about mouse numbers and data presentation were resolved.

Substantial agreement on core transcriptomic findings C3-C5 and C23-C26. OpenEval finds these claims well-supported with coherent evidence. Peer review R1 covers these same claims plus additional ones (C27-C29, C69-C70), describing all findings as 'convincing' and 'an important advance.'

Agreement on mechanistic model claims C43-C46 (and C6-C7 in OpenEval). OpenEval notes the model is plausible but causal relationships are inferred rather than demonstrated. Peer reviewers accept the interpretive framework as 'thoughtful and supported by the data' with appropriate discussion of limitations.

Agreement on ERV and PRR claims C36-C39 (and C42 in OpenEval). Both evaluations find these claims supported. OpenEval emphasizes the authors addressed annotation issues, while peer reviewers accept these findings as part of what makes P. leucopus unique.

Agreement on ISG expression claim C34 (and C35 in OpenEval). Both evaluations find these claims supported. OpenEval emphasizes the consistent pattern of reduced magnitude responses, while peer reviewers accept these as part of the overall convincing transcriptomic analysis.

Partial agreement on claims C30-C31 regarding rat validation data. OpenEval R2 covers C27-C31 finding all well-supported with statistical significance. Peer R5 covers C30-C31 and C33, commending the inclusion of rat data as validation.

Agreement on clinical observation claims C11-C12. Both evaluations find these claims supported. OpenEval emphasizes these provide phenotypic validation of transcriptional differences, while peer reviewers describe the data as 'convincing.'

Divergent evaluation approach for speculative claim C68. OpenEval rates C67-C68 as UNCERTAIN, noting the causal relationship between CD14 and LPS response is inferred not demonstrated. Peer reviewers rate C68 (and C50) as SUPPORTED, accepting the speculative nature as appropriately framed.

Divergent evaluation approach for speculative claim C50. OpenEval rates C50-C51 as UNCERTAIN, noting limited direct evidence for ERV suppression mechanisms in P. leucopus. Peer reviewers rate C50 (and C68) as SUPPORTED, accepting these as appropriate speculative interpretations with acknowledged limitations.

Agreement on macrophage polarization claims C69-C70. OpenEval finds these supported by multiple gene expression ratios showing M2 characteristics. Peer R1 groups these with broader transcriptomic findings (C3-C5, C23-C29) and describes all as 'convincing.'

Agreement on claim C33 regarding interferon-gamma and Nos2 correlation. OpenEval finds C32-C33 supported by literature and Figure 10 correlation analysis. Peer R5 includes C33 with rat validation data (C30-C31), accepting all findings without concerns.

Partial overlap on claims C27-C29. OpenEval R2 covers C27-C31 finding genome-wide and targeted RNA-seq data well-supported across species. Peer R1 includes C27-C29 within a broader set of core transcriptomic findings (C3-C5, C23-C29, C69-C70) described as 'convincing.'

Partial overlap on claims C6-C7 regarding ERV expression. OpenEval R6 covers C6-C7 and C43-C46, finding the mechanistic model plausible but with inferred causality. Peer R2 includes C6-C7 with C35-C39, accepting all findings as part of P. leucopus uniqueness.
OpenEval evaluated claim C13 (baseline hematology differences) as supported by data and consistent with prior reports. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addressed this claim.

OpenEval evaluated claim C22 (both species mount substantial transcriptional responses) as supported by genome-wide RNA-seq. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addressed this contextual claim.

OpenEval evaluated claims C47-C49 (ERV context from prior studies) as supported by citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addressed these background claims, though peer reviewers generally accepted the ERV findings.
